Flooding Disrupts Kuwaiti Oil & Gas Operations, Export Delays Expected

Severe flooding triggered by days of unseasonal torrential rain has disrupted oil and gas production and transport routes across key sites in Kuwait, according to industry sources and local authorities. The event, which began three days ago and is ongoing, has led to the temporary suspension of operations at several upstream plants and caused significant logistical challenges for export terminals.

The heaviest rainfall in over a decade has inundated access roads to major production sites in Kuwait’s southeastern region, including the Al-Sabah and Al-Murjan fields operated by National Petroleum Resources Company (NPRC) and Gulf Horizons Energy. Floodwaters have rendered critical infrastructure impassable, stranding staff and halting the movement of equipment and supplies.

“Production at Al-Sabah field is currently down by about 35% due to water ingress and limited access,” confirmed Omar Al-Mutairi, NPRC’s site operations manager. “Our teams are working around the clock to restore safe access, but conditions remain hazardous.”

Export operations at the Shuwaikh and Mina Abdullah terminals have also been affected, with tankers unable to dock amid high waters and debris. As of Thursday morning, loading delays of up to 48 hours were reported, and at least four export shipments are awaiting clearance.

A preliminary assessment by the Kuwait Oil Producers’ Union estimates that up to 210,000 barrels per day of combined crude and condensate output has been curtailed since Tuesday. “We are coordinating with the authorities on emergency drainage and road repairs, but the situation remains fluid,” said Union spokesperson Layla Al-Sanad.

Analysts warn that prolonged disruption could impact Kuwait’s supply commitments in the region. “Kuwait’s export infrastructure is designed to withstand typical seasonal weather, but this level of flooding is unprecedented,” noted energy analyst Rafiq Rahman. “If the rains continue, we could see knock-on effects in regional spot markets.”

Authorities have not given a timeline for the resumption of full operations, as further rain is forecast in the coming days. Industry stakeholders continue to monitor the situation as efforts to restore access and resume production intensify.
